newsitem.title: USA: Amgen sees Epogen growth rate slowing.
newsitem.headline: Amgen sees Epogen growth rate slowing.

text.p: Amgen Inc said Monday it sees a modest reduction in the 1997 growth rate of its Epogen drug, due to changes in Medicare's reimbursement policy.

Under the old system, reimbursement was authorized in kidney dialysis patients whose hematocrit level was above the officially approved level of 36 percent as long as there was "adequate medical justification." The new rules no longer accpept medical justification in patients with hematocrits above 36 percent, and denies reimbursement in patients whose hematocrit exceeds 36.5 percent on a 90-day rolling average.
Hematocrit level, a measure of red blood cell count, is about 40 percent in healthy patients.
Amgen said that some dialysis providers are temporarily witholding Epogen, which boosts red blood cell count, from some patients whose hematocrits exceed 36 percent.

The company said it does not expect the rules change to have a material impact on its financial results for the year. It said it remains comfortable with estimates of earnings of $0.70 to $0.73 per share for the second quarter and $2.80 to $2.85 for the year.
In 1996, Epogen sales rose 21 percent to $1.072 million.
